_what: The JS suites that are KNOWN to be failing on main. A RATCHET, not a permission slip: CI still goes red while this list is non-empty. What this file adds is the ability to tell a NEW failure from a standing one, which is the distinction register 300 says nobody could make.
_why: Measured 2026-08-24 (register 300): main had been red for over a week with no successful ci.yml run in the last 90, and the red had ACCRETED -- sampled backwards, 1 of 4 suites failing on 08-15, 6 of 6 by 08-22. No single commit to revert and no human watching the trend. A count that only ever goes up is invisible; a count checked against a committed baseline is not.
_rules: ADDING a name here is a deliberate act and needs a reason in the commit message. It is not a way to make a red build quiet.
REMOVING a name is the goal, and suite_baseline_check.js tells you when a listed suite has started passing so the ratchet can be tightened.

This file never makes CI pass. The JS suite step still exits non-zero while anything is failing -- see ci.yml. A permanently green build with 32 broken suites is the decay this whole exercise was about.
_baseline_taken: 2026-08-24, after register 300 phase (1): 49 failing / 16 inert -> 32 failing / 1 inert, of 437 suites.
_ratchet_log: 2026-08-24: -panel_spec. It was red on a DOC-ACCURACY claim, not a code defect: the spec said renderRecommendations was 392 lines and it is 422. The section header states the standard -- these claims "must be true now, not true when they were typed" -- so the fix is to make the claims true, and all 14 were re-derived from app.js rather than typed. THE REAL FIND WAS THE COVERAGE: the test checked ONE panel, and sweeping all 14 showed THREE out of tolerance with the largest invisible -- renderSeatPlan claimed 121 and was 252, MORE THAN DOUBLED with nothing watching; renderThreats +37. The check now covers every claim, and its fail arm was proven by planting the exact renderSeatPlan drift that hid (exit 1 with the poison, 0 restored).
